newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: VICTORIAN WEATHER FUELS FIRES
Two major fires and almost 50 grass fires have kept Victorian firefighters busy on a day of 39 degree heat and gusty winds.
More than 70 firefighters are at a paper factory at Cambellfield, north of Melbourne, where three metre high stacks of paper are burning fuelled by 40-kilometre winds.
And at Langwarren, near Frankston, the Country Fire Authority has all of its crews fighting a grass and scrub fire that is burning across an area of 50 hectares.
DANGEROUS CONDITIONS IN VICTORIA
Hot and windy weather is creating a fire risk in Victoria, not seen in the state for several years.
The Country Fire Authority says the fire danger index is at one of it's highest rates, because of the effects of wind, dry ground cover and the temperature of 37 degrees.
Spokesman Gary McQuade says Victoria's 70-thousand volunteer officers are on stand-by, with more than 20 small grass and scrub fires already today.
LARGE SUM STOLEN IN BRAZEN ROBBERY AT AIRPORT
Police say today's robbery at Sydney's international airport was a brazen and daring act considering the number of security guards and officers policing the area.

Early this morning, an unarmed man bound and gagged two women at the Thomas Cook foreign currency exchange and forced them to open the safe. A large amount of money was stolen but police refuse to give details as to the extent of the robbery.
Detective Senior Sergeant, Peter Miller of Mascot Police says while the women have received medical attention, they weren't hurt in the incident.
NSW GOVT REPS AT WIK MEETING
The New South Wales government has indicated it'll be sending representatives to the Cairns meeting on the High Court's Wik decision.
A spokesman from the Premier's office says representatives of the Aboriginal Affairs Department, and the Cabinet office's legal branch will attend.
Earlier today, the Premier indicated he was unwilling to enter the debate, suggesting there's a strong case for less talk, and more study of the High Court's decision.
He says there are too many opinions in the air on Wik.
TIGHT SECURITY AT GERALDTON TRIAL
The trial of accused murderer John Saint Claire Golightly is underway amid tight security in the Supreme Court at Geraldton.
The 54-year-old is charged with shooting his former friend and neighbour Wayne Tibbs last January.
A jury of six-men and six women, as well as three reserves, has been selected and the court has been adjourned for the defence to prepare for legal arguement on the admissability of some evidence.
Extra police have been called in and a metal detector has been installed outside the court for the duration of the trial which is expected to last four or five weeks.
TENSIONS MOUNTING OVER ACB TOP JOB
Tensions over the split between the Australian Cricket Board and former chief executive Graham Halbish have increased.

Mr Halbish, who says he's been banned from his former workplace, has released a further statement through lawyers, denying reports that claimed he barred chairman Denis Rogers from a sponsors meeting.
Mr Halbish says it's not true and he would never confront the ACB chairman in that way.
In today's statement, Mr Halbish says he wanted to settle the terms of his parting without acrimony, but couldn't stand by to see his reputation "besmirched"
Mr Halbish was sacked by the ACB last Wednesday.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
